detail.readme:
Community Scripts — Proxmox VE

One-command installations for services, containers and VMs on Proxmox VE
A community project — built on the foundation of @tteck's original work

--- ## What is this? **The canonical application scripts.** More than 700 of them, covering home automation, media, networking, databases, monitoring, security and developer tooling. Paste one command into your Proxmox shell and the container or VM is built, configured and running. A script only describes *what* to install. Creating the container, asking the questions and handling the errors is the job of the shared engine in [core](https://github.com/community-scripts/core), which every script loads at start-up. The same scripts run unchanged on an Incus host through [the Incus repository](https://github.com/community-scripts/Incus). Ready-made commands for every application are on [community-scripts.org](https://community-scripts.org). --- ## Getting started 1. Go to **[community-scripts.org](https://community-scripts.org)** 2. Search for the service you want — Home Assistant, Nginx Proxy Manager, Jellyfin 3. Copy the one-line install command from the script page 4. Open your **Proxmox shell** and paste it 5. Choose **Default** or **Advanced** and follow the prompts Each script page lists what the container includes, the default resources and the post-install notes. > These commands run as root on your host. Every script is readable in this > repository, and each script page links to its source — read it before you > paste it, as you would with any installer. --- ## How scripts work **Default** picks sensible resources and asks only what it has to. Most installs finish in a few minutes. **Advanced** hands you container settings, networking, storage backend and application options before anything is created. Every container gets an `update` command. Type it in the container console: ```bash update ``` It updates the installed application and reaches settings that would otherwise mean editing config files by hand. VM scripts have no built-in updater — use the guest's own package manager. --- ## Requirements | Component | Details | | --------- | ------- | | **Proxmox VE** | 8.0 – 8.4, or 9.0 – 9.2 | | **Access** | Root shell on the Proxmox host | | **Network** | Internet access during installation | Virtual machine scripts need the same versions as containers. --- ## Repository map | Repository | Contains | | ---------- | -------- | | [core](https://github.com/community-scripts/core) | The engine — container and VM creation, the wizard, error handling | | **ProxmoxVE** (this repo) | Canonical application scripts, plus `tools/pve/`, `vm/` and `turnkey/` | | [Incus](https://github.com/community-scripts/Incus) | The same scripts on an Incus host, plus Incus VMs and host tooling | | [DevScripts](https://github.com/community-scripts/DevScripts) | Where new scripts are tested before they land here | --- ## Layout | Folder | Contents | | ------ | -------- | | `ct/` | Application scripts — the command you paste | | `install/` | What each script installs inside the container | | `vm/` | Virtual machine scripts | | `tools/pve/` | Host tooling: post-install, hardware passthrough, maintenance | | `turnkey/` | TurnKey Linux appliance helper | Application metadata — name, description, logo, tags — is managed on the website, not in this repository. Use the **Report Issue** link on any script page to request a change. --- ## Testing a fork or branch Engine and scripts resolve independently, so either can point somewhere else. Put the variable on the command itself — nothing needs exporting. To run your own copy of the scripts: ```bash COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOU/ProxmoxVE/my-branch \ bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOU/ProxmoxVE/my-branch/ct/debian.sh)" ``` A `ct/` script fetched with `curl` cannot tell the engine where it came from, so without that variable it would look for its `install/` half upstream. Only when you are changing the engine itself: ```bash COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_CORE_URL=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/YOU/core/my-branch \ bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/main/ct/debian.sh)" ``` A local checkout of core wins over both — point at it with `COMMUNITY_SCRIPTS_CORE_DIR`. --- ## Contributing This project runs on community contributions. New scripts, fixes, bug reports — all of it helps. | I want to… | Go here | | ---------- | ------- | | Add a **new** script | [DevScripts](https://github.com/community-scripts/DevScripts) — new scripts are tested there first | | Fix or improve an **existing** script | [Contributing Guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) — open a PR here | | Change how containers are built | [core](https://github.com/community-scripts/core) | | Report a bug or a broken script | [Issues](https://github.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/issues) | | Request a script or a feature | [Discussions](https://github.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/discussions) | | Report a security vulnerability | [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) | | Ask a question | [Discord](https://discord.gg/3AnUqsXnmK) | ### Before you open a PR - **New scripts go to [DevScripts](https://github.com/community-scripts/DevScripts), not here.** PRs adding new scripts to this repository will be closed. - Keep a PR to one fix or one feature. - A bug that also happens on Incus is an application or engine bug — say so in the report. - Read the [Contributing Guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) before your first PR. --- ## Core Team
